BudgetWise is a .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Web API with a React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind frontend for personal finance and budget tracking, used in the GitHub Copilot Workshop.

**Code style:** Follow C# naming conventions (PascalCase for classes/methods/properties; camelCase for locals/parameters); use descriptive names, focused methods, composition, C# 12 features where appropriate, and `var` when types are obvious. Place `using` statements inside namespace declarations. Use strict TypeScript, React hooks and functional components, focused/reusable components, Tailwind utility classes, semantic HTML, and accessibility best practices (ARIA, keyboard navigation). Avoid inline styles; prefer Tailwind classes. Prefer clarity, beginner-friendly code, and best practices over cleverness; explain .NET Core and React concepts in comments.

**Backend/API:** Use constructor dependency injection and appropriate service lifetimes. Use minimal APIs or controllers consistently; keep business logic in services. Design RESTful endpoints with plural resource nouns, appropriate HTTP methods/status codes, resource ID path variables, and query parameters for filtering/search. Return `IActionResult` or typed results; never return null from endpoints. Validate inputs with Data Annotations or FluentValidation; use separate immutable `record` DTOs with validation annotations and explicit domain/DTO mapping. Return meaningful errors, consistent camelCase JSON, and proper Content-Type headers. Use built-in middleware where appropriate. Use nullable reference types, `required` for mandatory properties, property-based initialization, and navigation properties for related entities.

**Data:** Use in-memory collections for development/testing; populate realistic representative sample data via `MockData` class in `Data/MockData.cs`. Use thread-safe collections where necessary.

**Documentation/TODOs:** Add XML docs to all public classes/methods, including `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, and `<exception>` where applicable; explain WHY, not just WHAT. Add JSDoc for TypeScript. Mark incomplete features with `// TODO:` and a clear description; when implementing TODOs, follow existing patterns, write tests, and update documentation.

**Tests:** Use xUnit, React Testing Library, and `WebApplicationFactory<T>` for integration tests. Follow Arrange/Act/Assert; use descriptive names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`. Mock external dependencies in unit tests and API calls with MSW (Mock Service Worker) or similar. Cover success, failure, edge/boundary cases, accessibility, and user interactions (not implementation details); use Testing Library `screen` queries.

**Workflow:** Check similar code first; follow ASP.NET and existing frontend patterns; include error handling/validation; write tests with implementation; document public APIs; validate backend and form inputs; use typed responses and appropriate status codes; ensure frontend/backend coherence.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
❌ Do not use `any` type in TypeScript (use proper types or `unknown`)
❌ Do not create side effects in React component render functions

**Commands:**
```sh
cd budgetwise-app/backend
dotnet restore              # Restore dependencies
dotnet build                # Build the project
dotnet run                  # Start the API server (port 5000)
dotnet test                 # Run tests
dotnet watch run            # Run with hot reload
cd budgetwise-app/frontend
npm install                 # Install dependencies
npm run dev                 # Start dev server with Vite (port 5173)
npm run build               # Production build
npm run preview             # Preview production build
npm run lint                # Run ESLint
npm run test                # Run tests
```
